results.comment: [USER]  I'm soooo embarrassed for you. You lived your whole life thinking you were part of a religion that you don't even comprehend. It was written from Orthodox Archbishop Averky (Taushev), and they are the volumes that are widely circulated today in Russia which help others strengthen their faith.   Point being, I’m looking into circumcision specifically as my starting point. A quick glance over volumes II & III and trying to remember where I saw circumcision being spoken about...  I see two areas:  In the book of Acts, chapter 11 Volume II: the circumcised Christians at the time (Jewish Christians/Judaizers), were upset that Peter sat, lived, and ate with the “uncircumcised”. The Judaizers feverishly began to rebuke Peter for allowing this in his household, and it’s noted that this was only the start of Peter’s mission, and catechization of the faithful was not necessary at this time. “With this account, Peter did not directly answer the issues raised by the Jewish Christians, instead he showed them the will of God; to accept  those within the Church as brothers; and Peter’s account calmed them. (P. 57).  Volume III, p. 53 The Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Galatians:  I see that Galatia was a region in Asia Minor, neighboring Cappadocia, Lycaonia, Pontus, and other regions. The country was originally settled by Greeks, but soon the Jews moved to Galatia when Jews were forced out of Palaestine, Emperor Augustus gave special patronage to the Jews that moved to Galatia, which is mentioned by Josephus.   The Christian communities in Galatia began growing in large numbers, first with Paul, then Silas, and Timothy as they went through the cities delivering the news of the missionary journey from the apostles and strengthing their numbers.   P. 54. The purpose of this epistle was the apparently rabid Judaizers in Galatia, who began to insist on the necessity for circumcision, and other rites of the Old Jewish (Mosaic Law) for salvation. The Judaizers saw how lax Paul was, and his favor with Pagans, and they belittled his ministry by saying he wasn’t of Jesus Christ; he was only of his own selfish lips. Many Judaizers fell away by the time Paul arrived, (Gal 1:6). And he was astounded at how foolish and frivol the Judaizers were.   Paul immediately began to write to the people, to uncover their delusions. He wrote it with his own hand. (Gal 6:11).   Galatians is mapped out as follows:  1. Prologue, Paul’s greeting and introduction where he expresses the main theme. 1:1-10 2. A defense of Paul’s apostolic diginiry, which had been brought into question by the Judaizing false teachers. 1:11-2:1-21 3. A dogmatic section, in which Paul powerfully and completely reveals the main theme of his epistle — the reference of the Old Testament to the New, and the end of the importance of the Law of Moses (Jewish Law) after the coming of Christ the Savior. 3:1-29 & 4:1-31 4. A moral-instructive section, in which the foundation of the Christian life, separate of the Old Testament Law, is described. 5:1-26 & 6:1-10 5. A conclusion, in which concrete instructions are given concerning circumcision and reverence due to the Cross of Christ. 6:11-18  A few really cool points to summarize from the book of Galatians:   • Paul accounts his attendance to the first Christian Council of Jerusalem. (All Christians should additionally research the 7 important councils central to the faith).  • This Council declared Mosaic (Jewish Law) unnecessary in the life of a Christian.  • St Titus was one of the first uncircumcised (whole) men to be baptized and presented to the apostles, they did not require him cut for good reason.  • Paul’s epistle received sanction of all the elder apostles at this council. • The eldest of the apostles acknowledged how the Apostle Paul had a unique calling to preach to the uncircumcised; just as Peter’s calling was to the Jews.   ... SO MUCH MORE INFO. Christians who hadn’t already had a Jewish background, absolutely never cut for sure.
